title: Diegesis node template
description: A node template, assets/<namespace>/diegesis/nodes/<path>.json: node fields without an id; a scene node naming it with "template" starts from them.

vec3.description: [x, y, z] in Blockbench pixels (16 = one block).

scene.description: A Diegesis scene: what a station shows and lets the player touch. File: assets/<namespace>/diegesis/scenes/<path>.json. Coordinates are Blockbench pixels (16 = one block) relative to the block's corner, for a block facing north (its front on the -Z side); the library turns the scene with the block.

camera.description: Where the camera goes while the player works here.

work_plane.description: Height (pixels) of the surface carried objects and the held stack move over, usually the table top.

idle_visible.description: Draw the nodes while nobody works at the block (needs a block entity).

inventory.description: Lays the player's 36 inventory slots out in the scene instead of the vanilla panel on the screen.

interface.description: How the interface behaves and looks.

carry_planes.description: Levels carried objects rise to over parts of the scene, or areas closed to them.

inventory_drawer.description: Keeps the inventory in a drawer at a side of the screen; not together with inventory.

captions.description: How the lines of StationView.showCaption look.

clear_view.description: What stands between the camera and the station dissolves.

gains.description: What the player gets at the station flies into the inventory.

put_away.description: A right click with a stack on the cursor that nothing in the scene takes puts the stack back into the inventory, to the slot it came from while that is free.

placing.description: Lets items be put down anywhere on the scene's surfaces, turned and sized freely.

camera.description: The camera rig used while a player works at the station.

target.description: The point the camera looks at, scene pixels.

fov.description: Vertical field of view in degrees while focused; 0 keeps the player's setting.

transition.description: Seconds the camera takes to fly in and out.

inventory.description: A second shot the camera glides to while the scene's inventory is shown, and back when it hides.

seats.description: The view from each seat of the station, by seat id: a player in a seat sees that shot. Who has no seat, or a seat without a shot, sees the rig's own.

glances.description: Other places the player's look can go to: the cursor resting at an edge of the screen, or code, glides the camera there and back.

neighbors.description: Going over to a station standing next to this one: the cursor resting at the edge of the screen on its side flies the camera there.

gains.description: What the player gets at the station, seen going into the inventory; every field is optional.

enabled.description: A stack that comes into the inventory, other than from the player's own cursor, flies from the station to its slot, which bounces as it lands.

hold.description: Seconds a stack whose slot the drawer does not show stands next to the drawer.

sound.description: A soft pop as it lands.

count.description: "+N" shows how many came: rising from the slot, or beside the stack by the drawer.

camera_neighbors.description: Going over to neighbouring stations without leaving; every field is optional.

enabled.description: Neighbours are reachable from this station, and this station from theirs.

range.description: How far another station may stand, blocks along the floor; one up or down counts too.

zone.description: How far from the edge the cursor counts as being at it, as a part of the screen.

delay.description: Seconds the cursor must rest there, so that passing by moves nothing.

time.description: Seconds the camera takes to fly over.

hint.description: Draw a small arrow at an edge that leads to a neighbour, as the cursor comes near it.

hint_color.description: Colour of the arrow; its alpha is the strongest it gets, with the cursor at the edge.

keys.description: The movement and arrow keys go over at once to the neighbour on their side: A, D and left, right; W and up to the top edge, S and down to the bottom one.

camera_glance.description: A place the player's look can go to while working at the station.

id.description: Unique in the scene; StationView.glance and SceneEvent.Glance use it.

edge.description: The edge of the screen the cursor rests at to look here; without one only code does. One glance per edge, and not the inventory drawer's.

zone.description: How far from that edge the cursor counts as being at it, as a part of the screen.

delay.description: Seconds the cursor must rest there, so that passing by moves nothing.

target.description: The point the camera looks at, scene pixels.

fov.description: Field of view in degrees; 0 keeps the rig's.

time.description: Seconds the camera takes to get there and back.

back_on_take.description: Look back as soon as a stack comes onto the cursor here.

back_zone.description: The strip along the opposite edge that looks back, as a part of the screen; 0: no strip, only a taken stack or code ends the glance.

hint.description: Draw a small arrow at the edge the look can go to or come back from.

hint_color.description: Colour of the arrow; its alpha is the strongest it gets, with the cursor at the edge.

clear_view.description: Keeps the view of the station free while a player works at it; every field is optional.

particles.description: The world's particles dissolve; the scene's own never do.

radius.description: How wide the clear cone is at the station, in pixels.

soft.description: How far beyond radius things come back to full strength, in pixels.

captions.description: How the lines of StationView.showCaption look; every field is optional.

edge.description: The screen edge they sit at.

background.description: The band behind the text; a zero alpha draws none.

placing.description: Free placing: items of a slot group with placed() rules stand anywhere on these surfaces.

group.description: The slot group that holds the items.

item_size.description: Pixels the longest side of an item measures at size 1.

turn_step.description: Degrees of one notch of the wheel.

scale_range.description: The sizes a player can give an item.

scale_step.description: What one notch of the wheel changes the size by.

turn_speed.description: Degrees an item turns per GUI pixel of a drag.

stacking.description: Items can stand on each other.

block_models.description: A block item with a flat icon stands there as the block.

item_light.description: Items of blocks that give light shine on the scene, candles and torches burn.

light_radius.description: How far their light reaches, in pixels.

light_color.description: Colour of the pool of light they throw; alpha is its strength.

shadows.description: Items cast their shape on what they stand on.

snap.description: Positions are rounded to this many pixels; 0 keeps them.

preview_color.description: Colour of the see-through copy of the item in the hand.

place_surface.description: A level surface items can stand on.

aim_height.description: 0: the cursor points at the surface. Otherwise at a slope up to this height over the back edge.

wall.description: The z of a wall behind the surface: light in the room falls on it too.

camera_shot.description: Another view of the scene, in the rig's coordinates.

target.description: The point the camera looks at, scene pixels.

fov.description: Field of view in degrees; 0 keeps the rig's.

else.description: One object of the scene. It has a place, optionally a look, and behaviours. At most one of grabbable, slot, output, control (put others on child nodes). Children move with their parent.

id.description: Unique in the scene; behaviours and code refer to the node by it.

template.description: A node template, assets/<namespace>/diegesis/nodes/<path>.json, whose fields this node starts from: objects merge field by field, null removes a field. Built-in: diegesis:control/lever, switch, button, knob, slider.

repeat.description: The node once per cell of a grid: count [x, y, z] cells, each step [x, y, z] pixels further on, ids <id>_0, <id>_1... (x counts fastest; children get the same ending).

pos.description: Position relative to the parent (or the block corner), pixels.

rotation.description: Euler degrees, applied y (yaw), then x (pitch), then z (roll).

scale.description: A factor: one number, or one per axis.

visual.description: What is drawn; without one the node is an invisible pivot or hit zone.

collider.description: What the cursor can hit, in the node's own pixels; derived from the visual (or the role) when absent. Give plane-made vanilla blocks (torches, plants) an explicit one.

strokes.description: A press on the node starts a stroke: SceneEvent.Stroke every frame until the button is let go. Role-less nodes only.

precise.description: A mesh visual is hit only where its polygons are, not anywhere in the collider.

trigger.description: The collider is only a zone carried objects touch (SceneEvent.Contact); the cursor passes through it.

pickable.description: false: pure decoration without a hit box; the cursor and carried objects pass through it (a needle, a part drawn on a grabbable parent).

tooltip.description: Text next to the cursor while it is over the node: a translation key (shown as written when no language has it). Code can change it (NodeView.setTooltip).

grabbable.description: The player can pick the node up and carry it.

slot.description: The node is a place for the item of a station slot.

drop_zone.description: A slot group: a stack clicked or let go here goes into that group. The cursor passes through while nothing fits.

output.description: The node shows a station output; clicking takes it.

control.description: The node is a button, toggle, knob or slider driving a station control.

tank.description: Shows a station tank as liquid inside the node; with a spout the node pours. Combines with any role.

light.description: Shines on the objects around it and lights the work surface.

hidden.description: Starts invisible; code can show it (NodeView.setVisible).

extra.description: Free-form data for the mod's own code (NodeView.extra()).

visual.description: What a node looks like: exactly one of model, mesh, item, block.

mesh.description: A polygon model, assets/<namespace>/diegesis/meshes/<path>.obj; one unit is one pixel. Needs texture.

texture.description: The mesh's texture, a sprite of the block atlas: mymod:block/chess/king for assets/mymod/textures/block/chess/king.png, or any vanilla block texture.

model.description: A block model id, e.g. mymod:diegesis/flask for assets/mymod/models/diegesis/flask.json (every model under models/diegesis/ is loaded by itself; others need DiegesisClient.registerModel).

item.description: An item id, drawn like an item frame shows it.

block.description: A block state as in commands: "minecraft:lever[face=floor,facing=north]".

anchor.description: The point of the model (its own pixels) that sits on the node's position; the default is the centre of the model's bottom.

tint.description: ARGB colour multiplied into the model; alpha below FF makes it see-through.

translucent.description: The model has see-through textures (glass): drawn after solid parts, sorted.

double_sided.description: Faces are drawn from behind too: the inner walls of an open glass vessel.

glass.description: How clear the faces are where they look straight at the camera: they thicken towards a grazing angle, as glass does. 0 draws the texture as it is. Implies translucent.

grabbable.description: An object the player picks up with the cursor and carries.

lift.description: How high (pixels) the grip is held above the work surface.

sway.description: How much it leans while moving; 0 keeps it upright.

stay.description: Stays where it is dropped instead of flying back home.

grip.description: The point it is held by, node pixels (a vial by its top); the middle of its hit box by default.

plane.description: A plane of its own it moves in instead of the work surface (lift and carry planes then do not apply).

contact.description: The part that touches other things (a torch's flame), node pixels; the whole hit box when absent.

hold.description: auto: a quick click leaves it in the hand until the next click, pressing and dragging carries it until the button is let go; drag or click: only that way.

grab_plane.description: A plane a grabbable moves in; its grip follows the cursor on it.

point.description: A point of the plane, scene pixels.

normal.description: The plane's facing; [0, 0, -1] is an upright wall facing the block's front.

bounds.description: Where on the plane the grip may go, scene pixels; anywhere when absent.

carry_plane.description: With a height: a level carried objects rise to over an area (a vial goes up over a tall flask). Closed: an area objects may not enter (a torch stays outside a burner). Where planes overlap the highest wins.

from.description: One corner of the area, [x, z] scene pixels.

height.description: Height (scene pixels) of the object's grip over the area.

blend.description: Pixels round the area over which objects climb to it (or stay away from a closed one).

closed.description: Objects may not enter the area.

nodes.description: The grabbable nodes it applies to; all when empty.

slot.description: A place for an item of a station slot; clicked like a vanilla slot.
The station slot: "grid[4]", or "fuel" for index 0.

display.description: flat: lying on the surface; upright: standing, facing the camera side; floating: hovering and turning.

size.description: Size of the slot (drop zone, highlight) in pixels; also of the item without item_size.

item_size.description: Size of the shown item, when it differs from the slot's.

counts.description: When the stack's count is drawn; hover keeps slots close together readable.

highlight.description: The square over the slot under the cursor; off for things that are no slots to the eye.

output.description: Shows a result the station logic computes; clicking takes it.

size.description: Size of the item and of the click zone, pixels.

control.description: A control the player operates with the mouse. Knob/toggle turn round axis from range[0] to range[1] degrees; slider/button move along axis by that many pixels. Axis, range and pivot are in the node's own space.
The station control (declared in the schema).

type.description: button: click, springs back; toggle: click flips 0/1; knob: turned; slider: dragged.

axis.description: Turn axis or travel direction. Defaults: button [0,-1,0], toggle [1,0,0], knob [0,1,0], slider [1,0,0].

range.description: Movement at the minimum and maximum value. Defaults: button [0,1], toggle [-25,25], knob [135,-135], slider [0,8].

circular.description: A knob is grabbed anywhere and turned by circling the mouse round it; false turns it by dragging up or right.

pivot.description: The point a knob or toggle turns round, node pixels (a lever's hinge).

base.description: What stays still while the node moves (a lever's plate, a slider's track); drawn where the node rests, not clickable.

smoothing.description: Seconds the node takes to cover half the way to a new value; larger glides (a gauge needle on a locked control).

tank.description: Shows a station tank as liquid inside the node.

inner.description: The space the liquid fills, node pixels.

round.description: The liquid is a cylinder standing in inner instead of a box.

spout.description: Where liquid leaves when poured, node pixels; without one the node only receives.

pour_range.description: How far (pixels) round another tank the cursor still counts as pointing at it.

pour_angle.description: How far (degrees) the node tips at most; it stops earlier once the liquid reaches the spout.

opening.description: Where poured liquid goes in, node pixels; the middle of inner's top when absent.

pour_height.description: How high (pixels) over the other tank's opening the spout is held.

emitter.description: Gives off scene particles; code can switch it (NodeView.setEmitting).

particle.description: A particle style: diegesis:spark, bubble, droplet, splash, steam, smoke, glint, dust, flame, or one registered with DiegesisClient.registerParticle.

velocity.description: Start velocity, pixels per second; turns with the node.

spread.description: Random spread of the start position, pixels.

color.description: ARGB tint; the style's own colour when absent.

scale.description: Size factor over the style's size.

in_liquid.description: Start anywhere in the node's liquid and end at its surface (bubbles); offset and spread are then unused.

light.description: The node shines on the scene (also while carried).

color.description: ARGB colour of the light pool on the surface; alpha is its strength, 0 draws none.

flicker.description: How much it wavers: 0 a steady lamp, 1 a wild flame.

offset.description: Where the light comes from, node pixels (the middle of a long lamp).

inventory.description: The player's 36 slots laid out in the scene, vanilla order: hotbar the row nearest the player, slots 9-17 the farthest; column 0 on the player's left.

pos.description: Centre of the slot grid, scene pixels.

rotation.description: The grid's turn in degrees (y, x, z); flat without one.

surface.description: A block drawn as a board under the slots; without one they float.

slot_color.description: ARGB colour of each slot's square; alpha 0 hides them.

show.description: toggle: hidden until Tab (Tab hides again), shown while an item is on the cursor.

inventory_drawer.description: The inventory in a drawer at a side of the screen: an icon sits there, pointing at the side slides the inventory out over the scene, and while it is out it comes first. Every field is optional.

align.description: Where along that side it sits: 0 at the start (left or top), 1 at the end.

icon.description: The item drawn on the icon.

icon_texture.description: A 16x16 texture drawn on the icon instead, e.g. mymod:textures/gui/bag.png.

hover_zone.description: How wide (GUI pixels) the strip along the side is that opens it; 0: only the icon does.

open_delay.description: Seconds the cursor must stay there, so that passing by opens nothing.

close_delay.description: Seconds it waits after the cursor left.

margin.description: Gap (GUI pixels) between the open drawer and the side of the screen.

style.description: panel: the vanilla inventory panel; minimal: dark see-through squares.

slot_color.description: Colour of a slot in the minimal style.

always_open.description: It slides out when the station opens and stays out, without an icon; Escape leaves the station at once.

compact.description: Only the stacks the station can use (StationView.setInventoryFilter), in rows of up to nine, the drawer no bigger than they are.

pouring.description: How pouring looks; every field is optional.

hints.description: While a vessel with liquid is in the hand, tanks that would take it are marked at their openings.

meter.description: A small bar next to the cursor shows how full the tank being poured into is.

stream.description: The liquid runs in a continuous stream; false leaves only drops.

stream_width.description: How wide (pixels) the stream leaves the spout at full flow.

interface.description: How the interface behaves and looks; every field is optional.

hide_player.description: Do not draw the local player's own body (others still see it).

inventory_panel.description: Without an inventory layout, show the vanilla inventory panel (stations with items); false shows no inventory.

show_counts.description: Write stack counts next to items in the scene.

highlight_color.description: ARGB colour over the slot under the cursor.

shadows.description: Carried things cast a shadow of their shape.

carry_lift.description: How high (pixels) the held stack floats over the work surface.

carry_stick.description: The held stack settles onto the slot under the cursor.

carry_sway.description: How much the held stack leans as it moves.

carry_margin.description: How far (pixels) beyond the block's sides carried things may go; no limit when absent.

sounds.description: The library's quiet sounds for picking up, putting down and controls.

hover_outline.description: Outline the usable object under the cursor.

camera_partial.description: The camera rig used while a player works at the station.
